name: de2-115
device_part_note: Quartus Prime 25.1std has FITTED three designs for this part from this repository (hw/de2-115/step{1_bringup,2_enet,2_host}, Timing Models: Final), and the fit placed 106-126 pins at locations cross-checked against the Terasic user manual by common/make_pins.py -- a package pinout that would not all be legal for a different device. The part number is therefore no longer a guess. What is still NOT established is that any PARTICULAR physical board carries it: Terasic has shipped more than one DE2-115 revision, so check your own board's System Builder output before programming anything that drives a shared bus.
notes: fsm_encoding_pragma is intentionally null: Quartus has no single universally-reliable inline SystemVerilog attribute equivalent to Vivado's fsm_encoding -- it is normally set via the Quartus Assignment Editor / a .qsf assignment instead, not inline SV. emit_parser.py omits the pragma line and writes an explanatory comment when this is null. ram_style_pragma ('ramstyle = "M9K"') is Quartus's standard inline RAM-style attribute. Quartus Prime 25.1std IS installed on this machine now and the table memory measurement below was made with it, but this pragma itself has not been isolated in a before/after run. shift_reg_pragma: Quartus otherwise packs processing_generated's per-stage forwarding registers (the _s1.._sN chains) into M9K-based shift registers (altshift_taps); their RAM read latency sat on the design's critical path from the first synthesis run. Measured on load_balance_xsa (selftest top): recognition ON 66.1 MHz / 23.9K LE, OFF 71.3 MHz / 25.5K LE. Applied as a module attribute on processing_generated.
